messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: The viscous friction force depends on the angular velocity of the oscillating body and the damping coefficient of the surrounding fluid. Fluid properties such as density and kinematic viscosity directly influence the magnitude of the resistive torque. Torque due to viscous drag is proportional to the angular velocity, characterizing it as a velocity-dependent resistive effect. Effect sizes must be evaluated, and the viscous term should be included in the physical pendulum model when the oscillation occurs in a fluid or when amplitude decay is observable over successive cycles. Cycles of damped oscillation show a measurable energy loss, confirming that viscous friction is a relevant parameter in the equation of motion.
